scope: Finite31-family core utility inventory plus a linked exact70-module source-tree ownership index. Neither is universal method/type/algorithm completeness or Java SE conformance.
source_evidence_semantics: A source declaration and exported module package prove discoverable ownership at the pinned baseline, not execution, complete behavior, benchmarks or target admission.
candidate_semantics: New candidate API names are design/implementation inputs until their exact source, recipe and runtime receipts are recorded. No candidate is marked implemented or qualified by this inventory.

families.baseline_functionality: Null checks, equality/deep equality, hashing and checked index/range helpers have an existing public utility owner.
families.remaining_scope: Preserve overload resolution, lazy exception-message suppliers and exception precedence. A complete donor-method union is not established by this source inventory.

families.baseline_functionality: The integrated public Strings utility already contains null/blank/default, affix, padding, repetition and other String convenience operations; String retains payload and semantic ownership.
families.remaining_scope: Retain the existing merged utility and its source-first recipe. Additional Unicode, regex and donor method coverage needs operation-specific evidence; no replacement String representation is introduced here.

families.baseline_functionality: Existing public sort, search, copy, comparison, mismatch, range, fill and stream entry points operate on ordinary JDK arrays.
families.remaining_scope: Array/index/mask algorithms remain subject to reified component types, ArrayStoreException, overlaps, bounds, stable occurrence order and JNI lifetime rules. Full new utility coverage is not claimed.

families.baseline_functionality: Existing Collections sorting/searching and checked, unmodifiable, synchronized and sequenced wrappers keep their current contracts.
families.remaining_scope: Live filtered views, explicit stable sorted views and primitive mask selection are new direct-JDK candidates. Existing com.m3 collection views are donor/proving-ground owners, not proof of java.util integration.

snapshot_algorithm_selection.retained_snapshot_storage: Object[] values plus offset, length and reverse window state
snapshot_algorithm_selection.transient_filtering_storage: long[] mask and selected int[] physical indexes during capture
snapshot_algorithm_selection.qualification_boundary: Separate receiving receipts retain the rejected source and whole-call measurements. No general CPU/allocation speedup, default-native promotion or product-image qualification is claimed by this naming catalogue.

families.utility_entry_point: Distributed protocols; no public java.util.Iterators at the baseline
families.baseline_functionality: Iterator, ListIterator, primitive iterators and Enumeration define traversal, cursor and mutation contracts.
families.remaining_scope: A general Iterators utility entry point is a discoverability gap. Filter/concatenation helpers require explicit lookahead, remove, exhaustion and exception-demand semantics before addition.

families.baseline_functionality: Factories adapt arrays, collections and iterators into spliterators and back.
families.remaining_scope: New filtered projections must drop unjustified SIZED/SUBSIZED and preserve only valid encounter-order, comparator, DISTINCT and NONNULL characteristics.

families.utility_entry_point: Public Stream/primitive Stream factories and StreamSupport; existing Streams class is package-private
families.baseline_functionality: Existing object/primitive pipelines and StreamSupport supply creation and execution ownership.
families.remaining_scope: The proposed public Streams helper must preserve single-use/laziness, short-circuiting, encounter order, close-handler composition and callback failures. Public widening is not inferred from the existing private helper.

families.baseline_functionality: Existing collector factories define accumulation, combination, finishing and downstream composition.
families.remaining_scope: Temporary/virtual collectors remain separate proposed semantics unless their lifetime, associative combination, characteristics and materialization contracts are specified and tested.

families.utility_entry_point: Composition methods on functional interfaces; no public java.util.function.Functions at baseline
families.baseline_functionality: The functional interfaces retain identity, compose/andThen and predicate combinator APIs where defined.
families.remaining_scope: A general Functions helper is a discoverability gap. Reuse interface combinators and preserve short-circuit order, capture identity and callback exception propagation.

families.utility_entry_point: Array/Modifier/Proxy are existing focused utilities; general Reflection helper is a candidate
families.baseline_functionality: Reflection members, array operations, modifier checks and proxy construction remain in java.lang.reflect.
families.remaining_scope: The current Reflection candidate is limited to type and metadata inspection. Member discovery and invocation remain on the existing caller-sensitive owners; no access-check bypass or invocation facade is added. Full metadata contract and product-image qualification still require independent receipts.

families.baseline_functionality: Class identity, loading, member discovery and per-class associated values already have JDK owners.
families.remaining_scope: A single Classes convenience entry point is not present. Any future helper must preserve defining-loader identity and avoid accidental initialization or strong-loader retention; related reflection methods belong to the candidate Reflection owner.

families.baseline_functionality: Lookup, handle combinators, signatures and variable access-mode contracts have existing public owners.
families.remaining_scope: Preserve Lookup authority, exact/adapted invocation distinction and VarHandle memory modes. A method-by-method donor superset has not been qualified.

families.utility_entry_point: No general public IOUtils at baseline; candidate java.io.IOUtils
families.baseline_functionality: Stream/reader/writer methods own byte and character transfer, reads, writes, buffering and resource lifecycle.
families.remaining_scope: New IOUtils methods need exact partial-read/EOF, zero-progress, byte-versus-character, charset, checked-exception, flush and close-ownership contracts. Reuse existing transfer owners where possible.

families.baseline_functionality: Existing provider-aware file metadata, creation, copying, reading, writing and traversal utilities remain authoritative.
families.remaining_scope: Do not replace provider semantics or silently change link following, atomicity, permissions, stream closure or large-file behavior. Full donor filesystem-utility coverage is not established.

families.baseline_functionality: Path construction and path value operations use the owning filesystem provider.
families.remaining_scope: Preserve platform/provider-specific normalization and URI rules. Path helpers must not treat lexical normalization as filesystem identity or authorization.

families.utility_entry_point: Public buffer factories and methods; no general Buffers utility at baseline
families.baseline_functionality: Existing buffers define position, limit, mark, slicing/duplication, order and direct/read-only storage.
families.remaining_scope: A general buffer utility is a discoverability gap. Bulk helpers must preserve offset, position/limit, read-only and byte-order rules and account for native lifetime.

families.baseline_functionality: Channels adapts byte channels and streams/readers/writers; concrete channels own blocking and transfer behavior.
families.remaining_scope: Preserve partial transfer, interruption/asynchronous close, position, blocking and ownership semantics; generic I/O helpers cannot assume every channel always makes progress.

families.utility_entry_point: ResourceBundle and ClassLoader discovery; AutoCloseable lifecycle protocol
families.baseline_functionality: Localized resources, loader resources and scoped closure have existing distinct public owners.
families.remaining_scope: There is no one general resource helper. Resource discovery and I/O lifetime are separate contracts; suppression ordering and caller-owned resources must remain explicit.

families.baseline_functionality: Charset lookup/constants and incremental encoders/decoders own text-to-byte semantics.
families.remaining_scope: Preserve replacement/report/ignore policy, stateful encoding and incomplete trailing input. No platform-default charset is silently substituted by new helpers.

families.utility_entry_point: Existing java.util.regex.Pattern/Matcher for characters; additive TokenPattern/TokenMatcher candidates for object-token sequences
families.baseline_functionality: Pattern compilation, quoting, matching, finding, groups and replacement remain canonical regex APIs.
families.remaining_scope: Token builders are a finite object-predicate/capture/repetition API. They do not supply a lexer, textual grammar, backreference/lookaround builders or the full T-Rex language. Existing backtracking and stack costs remain; full fork-image, platforms and performance acceptance are pending.

declaration_tokens: public static <T> TokenPattern<T> token(Predicate<? super T> predicate)
public static <T> TokenPattern<T> sequence(TokenPattern<? super T>... expressions)
public TokenPattern<T> repeat(int minimum, int maximum, Quantifier quantifier)
public TokenMatcher<T> matcher(List<? extends T> input)
public TokenMatcher<T> reset(List<? extends T> tokens)
public TokenMatcher<T> region(int start, int end)
public record Span(int start, int end)

token_sequence_extension.source_evidence: Exact frozen product SHA and declaration tokens; executed contracts remain in a separate source-bound receiver packet.

families.utility_entry_point: Numeric type factories and static helpers; no general Numbers utility at baseline
families.baseline_functionality: Parsing, formatting, exact big-number arithmetic and floating-point classification have existing typed owners.
families.remaining_scope: A general Numbers helper is a discoverability gap. Overflow, precision, scale, signed zero, NaN and unsigned interpretation need explicit per-operation contracts.

families.baseline_functionality: Existing numeric functions, exact integer operations and floating-point utilities remain public owners.
families.remaining_scope: Do not conflate Math and StrictMath reproducibility guarantees; additional algorithms require accuracy/domain and overflow proof.

families.baseline_functionality: Existing bit vectors, shifts, masks, population counts and zero-bit operations provide reusable primitive machinery.
families.remaining_scope: A single Bits utility is not present. New indexed-mask operations must define logical bounds, unused high bits, signed shifts, aliases and mutation transaction boundaries.

families.utility_entry_point: Focused java.time factories, TemporalAdjusters and DateTimeFormatter
families.baseline_functionality: Clock, timeline, calendar, duration, adjustment and formatting owners remain distinct.
families.remaining_scope: A single Time/DateTimes utility is not present; preserve zone/DST, chronology, parsing/resolution and injected-clock semantics rather than flattening them into one rule.

families.baseline_functionality: Executor factories, asynchronous stages, timing, parking and threads have existing public owners.
families.remaining_scope: New convenience functions need cancellation/interruption, publication, ordering and progress guarantees. Source inventory does not prove linearizability, lock freedom or safe parallel collection mutation.

families.baseline_functionality: Process construction, handles, descendants, streams and exit observation retain existing ownership.
families.remaining_scope: A Processes helper is a discoverability gap. Preserve argument boundaries, environment handling, stream draining, cancellation and process lifecycle; do not introduce shell interpolation.

families.baseline_functionality: Protocol-independent addressing and HTTP client operations already span their owning JDK modules.
families.remaining_scope: A general network helper is not present. Keep URI escaping distinct from form encoding; preserve redirects, timeouts, DNS, TLS and resource ownership. HttpClient stays in java.net.http, not java.base.

families.utility_entry_point: Existing ZIP/JAR owners; no general Archives utility at baseline
families.baseline_functionality: Archive reading/writing and JAR metadata have existing stream/file owners.
families.remaining_scope: A general archive utility is a discoverability gap. Define entry-name handling, duplicates, sizes, CRC, random versus sequential access, ownership and extraction limits before implementation.

families.baseline_functionality: Provider-selected digest and MAC implementations retain their own state and algorithm identities.
families.remaining_scope: A digest convenience helper is not present. Preserve algorithm/provider choice, byte encoding, key ownership and mutable-instance confinement; hashing is not encryption.

families.utility_entry_point: DriverManager and RowSetProvider factories with JDBC interfaces
families.baseline_functionality: JDBC connection/statement/result ownership remains in java.sql and RowSetProvider in java.sql.rowset.
families.remaining_scope: A general JDBC helper is not present. Transactions, resource closure, parameter binding, batching and driver behavior need explicit contracts; no database implementation belongs in java.base.

families.baseline_functionality: Module resolution, layers, descriptors and service discovery remain JDK-owned.
families.remaining_scope: A general Modules helper is not present. Preserve readability/exports/opens, defining layers, caller authority and service-loading effects; do not infer permission from metadata.

qualification.phase_rule: Preserve the existing String -> arrays -> collections -> AST/compiler -> remaining families qualification plan.

internal_receiving_candidates.contract: Live filtered wrappers and sorted projections. Detached snapshots retain one captured visible Object[] with offset/reverse windows; sorting reuses Arrays.sort. Primitive masks and selected physical indexes are construction intermediates, not a permanent redundant permutation. No public companion type.
Two-pass clipped long[] mask selection produces detached ascending int[] physical positions. Java remains default; diagnostic native startup opt-in may fall back on missing symbol.
internal_receiving_candidates.native_declaration: static native int[] selected0(long[] words, int fromInclusive, int toExclusive);

internal_receiving_candidates.contract: Exact Java half-open range semantics, bounded GetLongArrayRegion and SetIntArrayRegion, no callbacks or retained input. Stock-JDK patched-module plus exact C testing does not qualify a built product image or platforms.
